answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable membership bond before it can earn or vote; rewards accrue only while the bond remains locked, and proven fraud burns it. A newcomer can still join, but multiplying identities means buying and immobilizing more capital, while a glacier of fake accounts risks losing every bond when one coordinated deception is exposed. The bond does not prove a person is unique; it makes Sybil influence costly. A sonnet or a trellis of fabricated profiles cannot bypass that price.
